title: Hetero Launches Generic Twice-Yearly HIV Prevention Injection in Africa

contentHtml:
New Delhi: Pharmaceutical manufacturer Hetero on Thursday said it has started phased shipments of generic injectable lenacapavir for HIV prevention to Africa, with plans to initially supply 3,00,000 vials to Zambia, Uganda, and Zimbabwe.

Introduced under the brand names Lexapir and Capvic, the twice-yearly injectable is recommended by the World Health Organization as an additional pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) option.

Hetero expects to introduce its generic oral initiation tablets by January 2027, with Gilead supplying them in the interim.

Hetero plans to supply the drug to 10 additional African nations in early 2027 and expand across low- and middle-income countries. It also plans an India launch over the coming months, subject to applicable regulatory approvals, a statement said.

"With an annual production capacity of 15 million vials of generic lenacapavir and the ability to expand further, we are ready to support wider access to HIV prevention across Africa," said Vamsi Krishna Bandi, Managing Director, Hetero Group of Companies.

He added that lenacapavir presents an extraordinary opportunity to "avert new HIV infections on a scale that could reshape Africa's public-health future".

Hetero's generic injectable lenacapavir and oral initiation tablets have received a Global Fund Expert Review Panel recommendation, enabling procurement in Zimbabwe through the United Nations Development Programme using Global Fund financing, the statement said.

Source : PTI
